history.p: Among the works that Scheibe composed during his early years in Leipzig are a few Magnificats and Sanctus settings. The present Magnificat was presumably commissioned by the cantor of Neukirche, Carl Gotthelf Gerlach, and was performed there in 1732. It thus belongs to one of Scheibe’s earliest surviving works. It has been argued that the settings of Magnificat, which were copied by students of the Thomasschule, were most likely not only performed in Neukirche but indeed also by Johann Sebastian Bach at the Thomaskirche. The framework of the present Magnificat is rather unusual as Scheibe chose to employ a solo Canto and Alto rather than the choir and included even a recitative ('Quia respexit humilitatem'). The work does not seem to appear in the Breitkopf catalogues though it clearly originates from the Breitkopf firm being one of their master copies in the 1760s. The firm most likely obtained Scheibe’s autograph manuscript score as well as the performance material following the death of Gerlach in 1761. Together with other sacred music, it was later sold to the collector O.K.F. von Voß-Buch and listed in his thematic catalogue as being by Giannettini 'no. 237'.

physDesc.watermark: the emblem 'WELENAV' and countermark 'S' is visible (Cammarota, Appendix C, nos. 30/30a).
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o; upright format consisting of two nested bifolios; music (fols. 1r–4r), blank page with staves (fol. 4v); in all 2 bifolios. Hand-ruled paper, 28 staves on fols. 1r–2r, 3r–4v, and 27 staves on fols. 2v (6 mm; single rastrum used) in light brown ink and music in black ink; a few staves have not been used. An autograph ink working manuscript. Bound with other sacred works all derived from the Breitkopf firm through Gerlach and later acquired by Voß-Buch. No original folder.
The score was originally part of the Breitkopf collections and was first bound sometime during the nineteenth century.

physDesc.physMedium: Parts placed in the original grey-blue Breitkopf limp folder, which is heavily water stained, contains six instrumental and vocal parts. 'No. 3' appears at the top centre of folder fol. 1r; the figure has been cancelled and changed to '7'. In upper right-hand corner the Buch-Voß number ‘237. part.’ has been added in ink and below 'P. 4. Bogen. | St. 6. 1/2 Bogen.' The Alto part is missing.

A clean copy with some additions in ink relating to dynamics and one tempo indication which are autograph (Scheibe); they do not appear in any of the other parts.
